topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches and mechanisms of action.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment approaches including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, detailing their mechanisms of action, systemic toxicity, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Cell Cycle and DNA Repair Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cancer cell defects, including hormone receptor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint alterations, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Drivers and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeted therapies directed against hyperactivated oncogenes and kinases, detailing small-molecule inhibitor design as well as mechanisms of pathway bypass and resistance.

topics.label: Therapeutic Monoclonal Antibodies and Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the use of engineered antibodies to target cell-surface antigens, either through receptor blockade, immune-mediated cytotoxicity, or targeted delivery of cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the immune system's role in tumor control and detail advanced immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T-cell engineering.

topics.label: Clinical Challenges, Future Perspectives, and Treatment Progress
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize current hurdles in oncology such as tumor heterogeneity, historical trends in cancer incidence and survival, and emerging directions in personalized cancer medicine.
